page.title: Best Rugged Tablets for Field Work: Drop, Brightness and Battery Compared (2026)
page.h1: Rugged tablets for field work: which survives the drop and the sun
page.desc: Getac UX10, Panasonic Toughbook G2, Dell Pro Rugged 12 and Samsung Galaxy Tab Active5 Pro compared on drop height and test conditions, rated screen brightness and battery as sold.
page.answer: Short answer. For rugged field work, the Getac UX10 is the pick: a 6 ft drop rating while operating, IP66 and a 1,000-nit screen. The Panasonic Toughbook G2 matches the 6 ft drop at IP65; the Dell Pro Rugged 12 was drop-tested at 4 ft, and Samsung rates the Galaxy Tab Active5 Pro at 600 nits.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Drop height: the Getac UX10 and Toughbook G2 are rated for 6 ft. StorageReview drop-tested the Dell Pro Rugged 12 at 4 ft. 6 − 4 = 2 ft more, or 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5× the height. Samsung's 1.8 m (5.9 ft) applies only with the case on.
  • Screen brightness: 1,000 ÷ 600 = 1.67×, so the Getac and Panasonic screens are rated two-thirds brighter than the Tab Active5 Pro. The Dell is rated 1,200 ÷ 600 = 2× as bright. Notebookcheck measured the Samsung at 768 cd/m² (768 ÷ 600 = 1.28× its rating), which is still below the three Windows tablets' ratings.
  • Getac battery in Wh: 11.61 V × 4.07 Ah = 47.3 Wh standard. The optional pack is 10.8 V × 9.24 Ah = 99.8 Wh.
  • Panasonic battery trade-off: 68 − 50 = 18 Wh more (+36%) for 2.9 − 2.64 = 0.26 lb more weight, and about 15 h instead of about 11 h on MobileMark 25.
  • Dell second battery: 35.6 × 2 = 71.2 Wh for $3,498 + $30 = $3,528. With both packs, RuggedPCReview measured 13 h 51 min in PCMark 10 at about 200 nits.

Drop, brightness and battery: what each rating actually covers

Drop ratings are tested under different conditions. Getac states 6 ft (1.8 m) while operating and adds that results vary with configuration and accessories. Panasonic's 6 ft figure is 26 drops onto plywood under MIL-STD-810H Method 516.8 Procedure IV, run by an independent lab, and falls to 3 ft with the keyboard attached. Dell's product page gives no drop height; StorageReview ran repeated 4 ft drops onto plywood over concrete, and RuggedPCReview lists a 48-inch transit drop. Samsung's footnote says the Tab Active5 Pro takes 1.8 m with the case on. If you plan to use it bare, you have no published drop figure.

Brightness: rated versus measured. Getac and Panasonic both rate their screens at 1,000 nits. Dell rates 1,200, and RuggedPCReview measured 1,320. Samsung rates the Tab Active5 Pro at 600 nits, and Notebookcheck measured 768 cd/m² peak. Samsung also notes that its No Battery Mode lowers screen brightness, so that mode suits vehicle mounts rather than outdoor work.

Battery swapping is often an option you have to order. The Getac UX10 and Toughbook G2 stay on during a battery change only if you add the optional bridge battery. Dell builds in two hot-swap bays, but the $3,498 configuration ships with one bay covered. Samsung includes two 5,050 mAh packs and says you can replace one without rebooting.

On a tight budget: Blackview's store lists the Active 8 Pro at $289 and states MIL-STD-810H, IP68 and IP69K, −40 °C to +60 °C operation and a 22,000 mAh battery. Blackview's store page gives no drop height or screen brightness, so it isn't in the table above. It suits light-duty work where a short drop is unlikely, not pole or ladder work. {buy:blackview-active-8-pro}

Not recommended

The Dell Pro Rugged 12 in its $3,498 base configuration, for drop-prone jobs. It is the only tablet here with a published price, yet it was drop-tested at 4 ft against 6 ft for the Getac and Panasonic, and the base configuration has a single 35.6 Wh battery. If its 1,200-nit screen is the reason you're buying it, add the $30 second battery so both hot-swap bays are filled.
